In 2018, Bitvavo launched the first version of its digital assets trading platform, to bridge the gap between traditional currencies and digital assets. By offering transparent fees, a wide range of assets and an easy to use platform, Bitvavo is making the currency of the future accessible for everyone.

In two years' time, Bitvavo has established itself as the market leader in the Netherlands and one of the largest in Europe, with over one million users exchanging tens of billions of digital assets a year.

About the Role

Bitvavo is building dedicated product management for Crypto Custody, the team that keeps customer crypto assets safe and enables earning yield. As Crypto Custody PM Lead, you will own product strategy for our crypto safeguarding and transfer rails, working closely with Engineering (Crypto Safeguarding and Transfers) and Operations to balance security, compliance, growth and revenue.

Employment Setup

This role can be done fully remotely, or based in one of our preferred hubs: Amsterdam, London, Limassol or Vilnius.

What You’ll be Doing

  • Own the product roadmap for crypto wallet security, custody transfers and new asset listings

  • Partner with Engineering to ship hot and cold wallet security improvements

  • Drive the crypto yield roadmap, covering staking, lending, stablecoins and on-chain products, together with Operations

  • Set strategy for withdrawal fees, network fee policy and node infrastructure

  • Manage key vendor relationships, including custodians, validators and infrastructure providers

  • Track AuC growth and yield KPIs in partnership with Data

  • Represent Product in incident response for wallet and crypto rail security events

What We’re Looking For

This role requires genuine crypto experience, gained at a crypto exchange, custody provider or similar crypto native business. We are not able to consider candidates without this background.

  • 8+ years in product management, at least 5 of which should have been gained at a crypto exchange, custody provider or similar crypto native business

  • Strong technical grounding, comfortable discussing wallet security, blockchain fundamentals and infrastructure trade offs with engineers

  • Track record balancing security and compliance requirements with growth and revenue goals

  • Confident managing stakeholders across Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Risk, Security and Treasury

  • Solid understanding of crypto fundamentals, with custody experience a strong plus

Desirable

  • Experience with staking, lending or on-chain yield products

  • Experience with crypto custody providers or cold storage operations

  • Background in traditional finance custody or asset servicing

At Bitvavo, we believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation, foster creativity, and lead to better outcomes. We are committed to building a team that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve and creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, religion, ability, or any other characteristic. Join us and be part of a team that values and celebrates your unique contributions.

Bitvavo does not accept resumes from staffing, search, or recruitment firms without a signed agreement. If you send us a resume without such an agreement, we may contact the candidate directly without any obligation whatsoever and no fee of any kind will be paid should we hire the candidate.

What We Offer

At Bitvavo, we believe in attracting, motivating and retaining talented people through market-competitive offerings that go beyond compensation alone. To learn more about our total rewards package and the benefits we offer, visit our Life at Bitvavo page.

Groma is blending real estate and technology to unlock a new real estate asset class while making it easier for everyone – from institutional investors to the residents in our buildings – to participate in ownership. Our investor technology platform makes owning these assets accessible to a broad array of investors, with bespoke vehicles available to institutional and family office investors and our flagship vehicle, the blockchain-powered GromaREIT, available to everyone, with a special focus on enabling ownership for the residents in our buildings. Visit www.groma.com to learn more about us.

We’re looking for a Head of Ecosystem to lead the growth and development of the Monad ecosystem. You will define where we focus, attract exceptional founders and builders, and help teams move from initial exploration to successful deployment, and sustained growth. This role combines leadership and management with direct execution.

You will own ecosystem strategy, founder, and builder programs, working closely with Engineering, Developer Relations, and Marketing, amongst other departments. Your mandate is to build and grow a thriving on-chain ecosystem of builders on Monad, while ensuring they have the tools, relationships, resources, and support needed to build, launch, and scale successful applications onchain.

Who You Are

  • 7+ years of experience across ecosystem development, growth, product management, or business development in technology, fintech, or financial services.

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience in crypto or Web3, with a strong understanding of blockchain ecosystems, DeFi, and the factors that influence where builders and founders choose to build.

  • 2+ years leading ecosystem development, incubation, or growth initiatives, with ownership of strategy, execution, and measurable outcomes.

  • 2+ years of experience at an L1 or L2 blockchain, attracting builders, developing strategic collaborations, and supporting projects from initial engagement through launch and adoption.

  • 2+ years of people management experience, having built, scaled and managed a team.

  • 2+ years of prior entrepreneurial or startup operating experience. A track record of working closely with early-stage founders on product positioning, go-to-market strategy, fundraising readiness, and ecosystem connections or operating one’s own entrepreneurial venture.

  • Experience designing or managing builder support programs, such as grants, accelerators, incubation programs, or ecosystem incentives, with clear milestones and evaluation criteria.

  • Strong relationships across crypto founders, developers, infrastructure providers, and investors, and the ability to translate those relationships into successful collaborations.

  • Commercial and product judgment, including the ability to evaluate emerging applications, structure collaborations, and allocate resources against ecosystem priorities.

  • Experience leading cross-functional teams or programs, aligning technical and commercial stakeholders, and remaining directly involved in execution.

  • Clear communication and strong analytical skills, with the ability to represent the ecosystem externally and measure success through builder retention, application traction, and sustained on-chain activity.

What You Will Do

  • Set ecosystem strategy. Identify the applications, verticals, and markets where Monad has a compelling advantage. Translate that strategy into clear priorities, budgets, and measurable goals.

  • Attract and support high-quality builders. Build relationships with founders and builders, source promising projects, and lead their journey from initial engagement through deployment and growth.

  • Secure strategic collaborations and deployments. Develop relationships with builders, accelerators, users, investors, and operators that strengthen the network and expand adoption.

  • Build a complete ecosystem. Identify gaps in sectors and applications. Coordinate the deployments needed to make Monad a compelling place to build.

  • Lead grants and builder programs. Design and manage grants, accelerators, and ecosystem incentives, with clear selection criteria, milestones, and accountability for outcomes.

  • Help ecosystem teams succeed. Connect founders with support, like GTM advisory, funding opportunities, launch resources, and users. Develop repeatable support programs as the ecosystem scales.

  • Drive ecosystem go-to-market. Work with Marketing on application launches, campaigns, events, and founder stories that translate awareness into adoption.

  • Build and lead the team. Hire and develop the ecosystem function, establish effective operating processes, and maintain clear ownership across collaborations and programs.

  • Measure and improve performance. Track ecosystem health and resource effectiveness, adjusting strategy based on builder retention, application traction, and sustained on-chain activity.

Why Work with Us

  • Challenging problems. You’ll tackle deeply complex and technically demanding problems, with autonomy and impact.

  • Endless Opportunity for Impact. The Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) standard is ubiquitous, but existing EVM-compatible chains are slow and bandwidth-constrained. Monad’s core innovations offer developers and founders the best of both worlds (portability and performance) and are a game-changer to power global on-chain finance.

  • The right team. You’ll be part of a world class team, who are exceptional and highly-motivated.

  • Culture. We’re a lean team working together to achieve very ambitious goals. We are united in our culture of collaboration, low ego, and high-quality output.

  • Strong Ecosystem. The broader Monad ecosystem has attracted support from leading investors, builders and long-term contributors.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

Robinhood’s Money team is building the next generation of banking and spending products for all Americans, starting with jaw-dropping Credit Cards. Our team members drive never-before-seen products and features from concept to launch to hyperscale.

As Director of Partnerships for our Money team, you will own the end-to-end partnerships strategy for Robinhood’s financial services ecosystem, from originating and closing high-stakes deals to scaling the relationships and teams that power our most critical products.

This role is based in our New York, NY office, with in-person attendance expected 5 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. 

What you’ll do

  • Originating, negotiating, and closing high-impact partnerships with leading consumer brands, major retailers, and strategic partners to unlock compelling customer benefits, rewards, and experiences.
  • Lead end-to-end commercial negotiations with key partners, structuring multi-year agreements that cover commercial economics, legal, security, and privacy terms, always putting the user first.
  • Serve as the primary executive-facing relationship owner for Robinhood’s most strategic partners, driving quarterly business reviews, partner health metrics, and long-term roadmap alignment.
  • Partner directly with Product, Engineering, Design, and Research to translate partnership capabilities into product roadmap acceleration and new user-facing features at scale.
  • Build and lead a high-performing partnerships team, setting clear goals, developing talent, scaling the function, and driving operational rigor across partner onboarding, integration, and ongoing management.
  • Identify and lead strategic initiatives with partners that directly move team OKRs, improving economics, accelerating product delivery, and expanding Robinhood’s competitive position in financial services.

What you bring

  • Significant experience in partnerships, business development, or strategy within fintech, consumer technology, or financial services with a proven track record of closing and scaling complex, high-value deals from origination through execution.
  • Deep expertise in the financial services ecosystem: payment networks, banking infrastructure, embedded finance, and the business models that drive consumer fintech at scale.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead commercial negotiations end-to-end  including revenue-share models, API and data-sharing frameworks, and co-marketing structures with the cross-functional fluency to align Legal, Finance, and Engineering behind each deal.
  • Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to influence and build trust with both internal senior leadership and C-suite contacts at partner organizations.
  • An established network within major payment networks (Visa, Mastercard), top-tier banks, or adjacent fintech platforms.

Leadership expectations

Our ambitious roadmap requires a great culture shaped by exceptional leaders. Here’s what we expect from them:

  • Drive high performance by setting clear, focused goals, giving real-time feedback, stretching top talent, and scaling impact through focus, innovation, and tech.
  • Hire and retain top talent by setting a high bar, hiring only those who raise it, investing in onboarding, and addressing talent issues quickly and fairly.
  • Create community by connecting work to purpose, removing friction while prioritizing safety, building trust and inclusion, and leading from the front with integrity.

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
  • Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
  • Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
  • Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

About Us

Founded 20 years ago and headquartered in Chicago, the DV>DV Group of financial services firms has grown to more than 600 people operating throughout North America, Europe and Asia. Since spinning out of a large brokerage firm in 2016, DV Trading has rapidly scaled as an independent proprietary trading firm utilizing its own capital, trading strategies, and risk management methodologies to provide liquidity to worldwide financial markets and hedging opportunities to commodity producers and users. Now, DV group affiliates include two broker dealers, a cryptocurrency market making firm, and a bourgeoning investment adviser.

Overview

We are seeking a full-stack developer to join our risk team. This role supports the design, build, and operation of the in-house risk engine, which powers real-time calculation and monitoring of PnL, VaR, greeks, risk slides, and other key risk metrics.

The ideal candidate combines solid backend and frontend development skills with strong DevOps fundamentals and hands-on experience using AI tooling in day-to-day development. You will work closely with senior risk developers, quantitative analysts, and market risk analysts to turn financial models into reliable, production-ready applications and keep them running smoothly under live trading conditions.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Build and maintain real-time risk systems used daily by risk, traders, and executives, including:
    • 24/5 live PnL tracking
    • VaR and other exposure calculations
    • Web-based risk dashboards
    • Interactive analytical tools
    • Alerting and monitoring systems
  • Own deployment, CI/CD, and infrastructure for risk applications: containerization, pipeline automation, environment management, observability, and incident response.
  • Improve system reliability, performance, and availability, with a focus on low latency and stability during market hours.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to accelerate development, testing, documentation, and debugging.
  • Develop and enhance applications that integrate LLM APIs for automation, analysis, and workflow improvements.
  • Build responsive front-end interfaces for visualizing and interacting with risk metrics.
  • Collaborate with the risk team to understand requirements and implement risk models.
  • Write clean, well-documented, and tested code; participate in code reviews and design discussions.

Requirements

  • 4+ years of professional experience as a full-stack developer, preferably in the financial industry or proprietary trading.
  • Strong proficiency in Python for data processing, backend logic, and model integration.
  • Solid DevOps experience: Docker, CI/CD pipelines (e.g. GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins), Linux administration, and monitoring/logging tools (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana). Experience with Kubernetes or infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform, Ansible) is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience with AI coding assistants and agentic development workflows, and a practical understanding of how to apply them effectively and safely.
  • Experience integrating LLM APIs (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic) into applications, including prompt design, tool/function calling, and evaluation.
  • Experience with at least one modern JavaScript framework (React, Angular, or Vue).
  • Proficiency in SQL and a solid understanding of relational databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL) and/or NoSQL stores (e.g. Redis).
  • Understanding of data structures, APIs, and real-time data processing.
  • Familiarity with real-time data visualization.
  • Exposure to quantitative models or working with quants is a plus.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Benefits

  • Discretionary bonus eligibility
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • HSA, FSA, and Dependent Care Options
  • Employer Paid Group Term Life and AD&D insurance
  • Voluntary LTD, Life & AD&D insurance
  • Flexible Vacation policy
  • Retirement plan with employer match

All resumes submitted by search firms to DV via e-mail, the Internet, personal delivery, facsimile, or any other method without a valid written agreement shall be deemed the sole property of DV, and no fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by DV. DV is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

descriptions.job-1u6r1m5:
## About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

## About the Role

Polymarket ships fast. New products, new market types, new payment rails, new geographies: the pace is real and it does not slow down for anyone. The Customer Experience team's job is to make sure that speed does not come at the cost of the people using the platform. Right now, CX readiness for new launches is a gap we need to close, and this role closes it.

You will own launch readiness for CX end to end. That means getting into product planning early, building the readiness plan, standing up a small pilot support pod, and running it until the launch is stable enough to hand off to our scaled operation or external partners. You will write the playbook as you go, because in many cases nobody has supported this type of product before. The team you will work with spans support operations, enablement, and external partners, and you will be the connective tissue between all of them and the Product teams shipping new things.

This is a builder role. If you need a defined process to work within, this is not the right fit. If you are energized by figuring out how to support something that has never been supported before, and then making sure the next person does not have to figure it out from scratch, this is exactly the right fit.

## What You'll Do

  • Build and own the CX readiness plan for every new product, market type, and geography launch, from kickoff through stable handoff.
  • Embed with Product teams at the planning stage to surface support needs, flag risks, and make sure CX requirements are scoped in before engineering is done.
  • Stand up and directly manage pilot support pods for new launches, including staffing, tooling, and day-to-day operations during the incubation period.
  • Work with the Enablement team to produce training materials, SOPs, and QA criteria before each launch goes live.
  • Track contact rates, issue trends, and customer satisfaction data for newly launched products and report findings back to Product with clear recommendations.
  • Define the criteria for what "stable" looks like for each launch, and execute the handoff to scaled operations or external partners once those criteria are met.
  • Build the readiness framework for international expansion, accounting for language, regulatory context, and partner capability as Polymarket enters new markets.

## What We're Looking For

  • 4 or more years in support operations, program management, or product operations, with direct ownership of launch readiness or go-live planning.
  • Demonstrated experience launching new products, market types, or geographies from the support side, including building SOPs and training from scratch.
  • Track record of strong cross-functional partnership with Product and Engineering teams, not just coordination but actual influence on how products are built and scoped.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity: you have built processes where none existed and made good decisions without complete information.
  • Strong written communication, you can write a clear readiness plan, a crisp status update, and a useful post-launch report without someone editing it for you.
  • Organized and reliable follow-through: teams and partners depend on you to track details and close loops without being chased.
  • (Plus) Experience at a startup or high-growth company where the roadmap changed fast and you had to adapt your plans to match.
  • (Plus) Experience managing international or multi-geography launches, including working with external support partners across different time zones and languages.

## Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage
  • 401k match
  • Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories

Pay Transparency

Base salary range: $200,000 to $250,000, plus equity and benefits.

This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.
descriptions.job-1lahujx:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe’s Financial Crimes Compliance Risk Oversight (FinCRO) team is looking for a U.S. Regulatory Compliance Lead for our Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) business. You’ll own second-line oversight of Stripe’s U.S. BaaS products and bank-fintech partnerships. The work is practical and cross-functional: turn federal and state requirements and supervisory expectations into clear policies, controls, monitoring, evidence, and ownership.

What you’ll do

This role is focused on U.S. BaaS regulation. You’ll work across sponsor-bank and fintech responsibility mapping; BSA/AML and sanctions; consumer protection and fair lending; deposits and FDIC insurance representations; privacy, cybersecurity, incident response, and third-party risk; complaints and disputes; payment network and ACH rules; state money transmission and lending requirements; and regulatory exams, remediation, and change management.

Responsibilities

  • Own the second-line compliance framework for Stripe’s U.S. BaaS products (i.e., Capital, Issuing, and Treasury) and bank-fintech partnerships. Make sure responsibilities are clear across Stripe, sponsor banks, program managers, processors, and other partners.
  • Turn U.S. federal and state laws, guidance, enforcement actions, and supervisory expectations into practical policies, product requirements, controls, procedures, evidence standards, and monitoring.
  • Set and oversee controls for BSA/AML, customer identification and verification, customer due diligence and beneficial ownership, transaction monitoring, suspicious activity escalation, sanctions screening, and recordkeeping.
  • Oversee consumer and lending compliance for BaaS products, including UDAAP; Regulations E, Z, B, and DD; fair lending; FCRA; SCRA; FDCPA; complaints and disputes; adverse action; collections; marketing and disclosures; fees; account restrictions; and account closures.
  • Oversee deposit-product compliance, including FDIC insurance representations, Reg CC, pass-through insurance requirements, pooled or custodial structures, customer-level records, ledger integrity, reconciliation, and access to funds.
  • Define compliance expectations for privacy, cybersecurity, incident escalation, operational resilience, business continuity, data access, record retention, and an orderly wind-down of BaaS programs.
  • Provide second-line oversight on behalf of sponsor banks and other BaaS partners through risk assessments, due diligence, contract requirements, control testing, performance and complaint monitoring, issue management, and exit planning.
  • Review new U.S. BaaS products and material changes. Identify applicable obligations, control gaps, licensing implications, and launch conditions, then drive remediation to closure with clear owners.
  • Keep pace with U.S. BaaS regulatory developments and enforcement trends, assess what they mean for Stripe, and coordinate timely changes with first-line teams.
  • Help Stripe prepare for and respond to U.S. regulatory exams, supervisory engagements, audits, and formal commitments. Maintain defensible obligation mappings and evidence, identify gaps, and oversee remediation.
  • Work closely with Product, Legal, Risk, Engineering, Operations, Internal Audit, sponsor-bank teams, and other specialists. Clarify ownership, challenge control design and execution, and give leaders a clear view of risk and progress.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. 

Minimum requirements

  • At least 7 years of experience in U.S. banking, fintech, or financial-services compliance, including substantial work with BaaS, bank-fintech partnerships, embedded finance, or deposit, card, payment, or lending products.
  • A deep understanding of the U.S. regulatory framework for BaaS and how responsibilities are divided among sponsor banks, fintechs, program managers, processors, and other service providers.
  • Hands-on expertise across several relevant areas, such as BSA/AML and sanctions, consumer financial protection, fair lending, deposit and FDIC insurance requirements, third-party risk, complaints and disputes, privacy and cybersecurity, ACH or card programs, and state money transmission or lending requirements.
  • A track record of turning complex U.S. legal and regulatory requirements into practical policies, product requirements, controls, procedures, monitoring, testing, and evidence.
  • Experience with the full compliance control lifecycle: assessing risk and obligations, designing and implementing controls, documenting decisions, testing or monitoring, managing issues, overseeing remediation, and reporting to governance forums.
  • Experience reviewing new products and material changes, as well as supporting regulatory change, licensing analysis, exams, audits, enforcement remediation, or commitments to regulators and Boards.
  • Sound judgment, especially when ownership, regulatory precedent, or operating boundaries are not clear. You know how to separate second-line oversight from first-line execution and still move the work forward.
  • The ability to influence and coordinate across Compliance, Legal, Product, Engineering, Risk, Operations, Internal Audit, sponsor banks, and senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.
  • Clear, concise writing and strong documentation skills. You can explain complex BaaS requirements and control decisions to technical, business, governance, partner-bank, and regulatory audiences.
descriptions.job-1ybw1kd:
OKX will be prioritising applicants who have a current right to work in Hong Kong, and do not require OKX's sponsorship of a visa.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
 
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. 
 
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.
 

About The Opportunity

OKX is building out its equities and tokenized securities business. This is a post-trade and brokerage systems product role — you will own the layer that sits between our users and the securities markets: order management, execution, settlement, asset servicing and reconciliation.
We have strong crypto product and engineering talent. What this role brings is depth in brokerage architecture and securities market structure: how these systems are built, why they are built that way, and what breaks at scale. You will be the internal authority on that, and your judgment will shape decisions that are expensive to reverse.

What You’ll Be Doing 

  • Own the brokerage core — order management, execution and routing, instrument lifecycle and trading status, settlement and reconciliation.
  • Shape account, custody and clearing architecture, along with the operating model required to run it.
  • Own corporate actions and asset servicing end to end, in both conventional and on-chain form.
  • Define how securities risk and margin frameworks coexist with those of a 24/7 digital asset market.
  • Bring market structure, execution quality and regulatory requirements into product decisions early, before they become blockers.
  • Set the standard for rigour — write PRDs precise enough to build from, and lead alignment across engineering, risk, legal, compliance and treasury.

What We Look For In You 

Domain Depth
  • 5+ years in post-trade or brokerage systems product management. We strongly prefer candidates from internet and licensed brokerages — Futu, Tiger, Interactive Brokers, Robinhood, Webull, Longbridge — as well as clearing firms and brokerage infrastructure providers.
  • Architectural perspective. You have a clear view of where responsibility belongs across the order, execution, clearing, settlement, asset servicing and ledger layers, and of what goes wrong downstream when a boundary is drawn in the wrong place.
  • Depth across the order and execution path. Order types and parameters, state machine design, idempotency across an external execution boundary, cancel/replace and partial-fill semantics, timeout and exception recovery. This is the core craft of the role.
  • End-to-end ownership of at least one area beyond the order path — clearing and settlement, corporate actions and asset servicing, margin and risk, securities lending, or position and cash reconciliation.
  • Commercial and historical perspective. You understand how a brokerage actually earns, how each revenue line constrains the systems beneath it, and why the industry made the structural choices it did.
Ways of Working
  • Strong technical intuition. You are comfortable discussing system architecture and data flows with engineers. You do not need to be a developer, but you think with the rigour of one.
  • You design for the exceptions — the halted symbol, the timed-out counterparty, the partial fill, the corporate action mid-flight — not just the order that goes through.
  • You run programs, not just write specs. You produce rigorous PRDs independently, drive alignment across engineering, risk, legal, compliance and treasury, and own the full lifecycle from requirements through post-launch review.
  • You write precisely, and can make complex mechanics legible to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • High agency. You are comfortable taking an open question all the way to a shipped, reconciled system, and making calls with incomplete information.
  • Proficiency in Mandarin is required to communicate effectively with internal engineering and product stakeholders in the China-based R&D center.

Nice-To-Haves 

  • Product experience with margin financing or securities lending.
  • Exposure to tokenized securities, digital asset custody, or on-chain settlement.
  • Experience integrating with broker-dealer or clearing APIs, as either the integrator or the provider.
  • Hands-on experience with multi-jurisdiction regulatory frameworks — SEC/FINRA, MiFID II, or equivalent.
  • A track record of launching a brokerage product in a new market from zero.
  • Fluency in English to support communication with global product and business stakeholders.
  • Genuine curiosity about what happens when securities markets meet 24/7 markets.

Perks & Benefits 

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • Wellness and meal allowances
  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!


Please note that Hong Kong is a group-level service hub, and OKX does not carry on a business of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team and the role

The People Systems Operations Administrator supports the day-to-day work that keeps Stripe’s People technology running accurately and reliably. The role sits in the Service Delivery Center and works as part of the wider People Solutions team, with a close dotted-line partnership to People Solutions Systems Management.

You’ll own a defined set of routine tier 1 and tier 2 operational work across Workday and related People Systems. This includes monitoring support channels and system inboxes, triaging requests, completing repeatable administrative tasks, maintaining documentation, and routing complex issues to the right People Systems owner.

This is a hands-on operations role. It creates clearer separation between routine support work and the configuration, architecture, governance, and project delivery owned by the People Systems team.

What you’ll do

Support queue and request triage

  •  Monitor the Salesforce case management queue and Jira requests for People Systems work.
  • Triage incoming requests by urgency, business impact, data sensitivity, and defined support process.
  • Resolve standard requests using documented procedures, and route exceptions or higher-complexity work to the appropriate People Systems owner.
    Keep request records accurate and complete, including status updates, required approvals, supporting documentation, and clear handoffs.
  • Identify recurring request patterns and flag opportunities to improve documentation, self-service, or system processes.

Workday operations 

  • Monitor the Workday inbox for business process errors, stuck transactions, alerts, and other operational issues.
  • Complete routine Workday support tasks, including standard access requests, account maintenance, and operational follow-up.
  • Support Salesforce and JIRA run work and respond to common People Systems questions using approved guidance.
  • Help with recurring operational tasks such as account monitoring, account resets, and quarterly account reviews.
  • Support year-end activity, including schedule extensions, alert configuration, audit requests, and tracking follow-up items.
  • Assist with release readiness by reviewing assigned Workday updates, completing test steps, documenting results, and escalating issues found during testing.
  • Support recurring People programs, such as performance-cycle launches, using established runbooks and checklists.

Reporting, documentation, and Jira support

  • Complete standard reporting tasks and access-related requests where there is a documented process and appropriate approval.
  • Maintain runbooks, Trailhead content, standard operating procedures, and request templates so guidance stays current and easy to find.
  • Support data-quality checks and follow established processes to correct or escalate issues.

Partnership with People Systems

  • Work closely with People Systems analysts and engineers to understand support priorities, upcoming releases, recurring work, and escalation paths.
  • Provide clear handoffs for work that requires configuration changes, advanced reporting, integrations, security decisions, or policy interpretation.
  • Participate in regular reviews of queue trends, service levels, documentation gaps, and operational risks.
  • Build platform knowledge over time, with opportunities to take on more complex administration and configuration work as skills develop.

Minimum requirements

  • Experience in People operations, HR administration, systems support, service delivery, or another operations role involving high-volume, process-driven work.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly where accuracy affects People records, access, payroll, compliance, or reporting.

About Coinflow

Coinflow is the next-generation payment service provider revolutionizing global financial infrastructure with stablecoins, AI-driven fraud prevention, and instant settlement. In response to this growth, Coinflow announced a $25M Series A in October 2025—led by Pantera Capital, CMT Digital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, and Reciprocal Ventures—accelerating our mission to power the world’s fastest-moving businesses with innovative, reliable global payments.

Coinflow is proudly headquartered in Chicago, IL. Learn more at coinflow.cash.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Coinflow's risk and compliance function has grown quickly across the US, Canada, and EU, and it now needs to mature from a collection of jurisdictional efforts into a coordinated, defensible group-level program. As our first Sr. Manager, Compliance Program & Governance, reporting directly to the Chief Risk Officer, you'll build the infrastructure that connects it all: regulatory change management, governance cadence, sponsor bank management, audit readiness, remediation tracking, product/tooling development, and second-line control testing.

This role works as a direct extension of the CRO. The CRO is accountable for the program; you're accountable for making sure nothing falls through the cracks between intake and closure. When an issue lands (a sponsor bank finding, a regulatory change, an audit observation, a self-identified gap), you take it, build the plan, line up the right people across Underwriting, AML, Legal, Engineering, and Operations, and drive it to a documented close.

Plainly: the CRO should never have to ask you for a status update. You should be the one bringing it. This is a building role at a rapidly scaling fintech, with a direct path to shaping how our program operates for years to come.

To be clear about scope, this role does not own transaction monitoring tuning, alert investigation, SAR decisioning, or merchant underwriting; those sit with our existing first-line teams. It is not a regulatory expert role for any specific jurisdiction; the BSA Officer and the MLROs hold those mandates.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the policy, SOP, and control framework that governs the program across regions: version control, approval workflows, attestation tracking, and refresh cycles. Make sure it holds up under testing.

  • Harmonize policies across the US, Canada, EU, and future jurisdictions into group policy with local addenda where possible, and own the policy exception process end to end.

  • Build and run an independent second-line testing and monitoring program for BSA/AML controls (CIP, KYC, CDD, EDD). Own the testing calendar, sampling methodology, and documentation so we walk into exams and bank partner reviews with evidence already assembled.

  • Serve as the program-level owner for bank and payment partner relationships, integrating incoming requirements, controls, and reporting obligations into workflows that minimize disruption to first-line teams.

  • Pre-review bank onboarding due diligence responses before they reach the CRO, and standardize the partner escalation guide so relationships are managed consistently.

  • Own Risk change intake as the single front door for FinCEN, FINTRAC, EU AMLD, MiCA, sponsor bank, and card scheme changes. Triage, assign owners, and build execution plans. Nothing sits open without you knowing why.

  • Lead audit and exam readiness. Maintain evidence libraries, response playbooks, and document rooms; coordinate responses to internal audits, sponsor bank reviews, and regulatory exams; and drive findings through to closure.

  • Own the risk and gap register. Intake self-identified gaps and findings from partner due diligence reviews, assign owners, and drive items to closure with audit-ready evidence. If something is stuck, escalate before it becomes a finding.

  • Design and operate the governance cadence, including our Risk and Compliance Committee, and chase committee action items until they're done.

  • Prepare board-level reporting and maintain a command center that gives the CRO, CEO, and board a coherent view of program health across jurisdictions.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on tooling requirements that reflect our policies and SOPs, so workflows in our tools act as the SOP itself rather than a disconnected series of steps.

  • Own rollout planning, acceptance criteria, and training for new tools so Risk and Compliance teams are ready to adopt them on day one.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5–10 years of experience in compliance, risk, audit, consulting, or related program management roles, with at least three years in fintech, payments, startups, or banking.

  • Prior experience building or standing up a program from scratch or in a high-growth environment, not just maintaining a mature program at a large institution. Much of the work in this role exists today but is divided across multiple people and lacks structure; you'll turn it into a coherent, documented program.

  • A constitutional inability to let things sit open. You track your own commitments and other people's commitments to you, and you follow up before anyone has to ask. If a thread goes quiet for three days, you're already pinging it.

  • Comfort holding people accountable without authority. You lead through clarity, persistence, and a willingness to be the one who says "I still need this from you" for the fourth time, professionally, without flinching.

  • Strong project management instincts and a bias for visibility. You can hold five workstreams in your head, prioritize ruthlessly, and build lightweight structure (trackers, dashboards, standing updates) so everyone knows their responsibilities across every active project.

  • Compliance generalist fluency. You can read a regulation, a policy, or an audit finding and immediately understand what it asks for, even if the specific regime is new to you.

  • Strong judgment about what matters. You can distinguish a material risk from a cosmetic gap and escalate accordingly.

  • Based in or willing to relocate to Chicago; this role is in office four days per week.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Prior experience supporting regulatory examinations or sponsor bank audits as a respondent.

  • Experience with multi-jurisdictional compliance programs, particularly across US, Canada, and EU regimes.

  • Prior experience designing or executing second-line testing programs for BSA/AML or equivalent AML regimes.

  • CAMS, CRCM, CFE, or equivalent certification.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • The chance to be Coinflow's first compliance program leader and shape how the program operates for years to come.

  • Competitive compensation including base salary and equity.

  • Direct partnership with the CRO and regular exposure to Coinflow's founders, leadership team, and board.

  • Comprehensive benefits, including health and wellness coverage, 401(k), and flexible time off.

  • A clear path to people management as the function grows.

  • Real ownership: the mandate to turn distributed, multi-jurisdictional efforts into one coherent, defensible program.

The base salary range for this role is $180,000 – $210,000 USD + equity. The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, skills, qualifications, and business needs.

About the Role

We're looking for a Staff Frontend Engineer who operates across the full picture - someone who deeply understands how great web interfaces are built and how they perform, works autonomously, and translates that knowledge into exceptional web products and design systems.

Financial products are complex. Our users range from first-timers to power users, and the challenge of making that experience clear, fast, and trustworthy is one we take seriously. At this level, you're not just executing - you're bringing product intuition to the work, identifying where things break down, and making calls that shape the direction of what we build.

How you can make an impact:

  • Work autonomously across our web products, building high-quality UI with a strong point of view on how it should feel, function, and perform
  • Own and evolve complex, reusable components within the Aave design system - setting the standard for quality and consistency
  • Set the bar for frontend performance, from data loading, fetching and caching patterns through to server rendering and streaming
  • Bring product-level thinking to everything you work on - understanding user needs, business context, and technical constraints, whilst balancing them well
  • Collaborate with our talented designers, engineers, and product leads to bring clarity to ambiguous problems
  • Help raise the bar for the team through the quality of your work and the way you approach problems

Let's connect if you have:

  • Strong proficiency in React, TypeScript, CSS and system design and architecture
  • Deep experience with frontend performance engineering - measuring it, diagnosing it, and fixing it
  • Strong command of Next.js patterns for data loading, fetching and caching, and experience handling server rendering and streaming data to the frontend
  • Deep experience with component-driven design systems and component design patterns, and building for consistency at scale
  • The product sense to work without a detailed brief - you can identify what needs to be solved, not just how to solve it
  • A demonstrated ability to take complex UX problems - information-dense interfaces, multi-step flows, edge cases - and make them feel resolved and clear

Nice to haves:

  • An understanding of backend data handling
  • A feel for animation best practices when data is updating, and how that plays out in re-renders across a UI
  • Curiosity about web3 and DeFi is a plus; you don't need to be an expert, but genuine interest in the space goes a long way
  • Curiosity about AI and its use in product engineering and daily workflows
Haven’t quite met all the criteria? Let’s not miss out on the chance to speak. Whilst you might not meet every single requirement, you might bring other, more exciting skills to the companies!
